guide.label: Guide
guide.title: Guide
guide.intro: The guide walks you through the few knobs that matter most for this job, moving each one on the map so you can see what it does.
guide.needs_code: This needs a code change. Muse Code writes it in a sandbox and a verify run checks it.
guide.pin.help: Put it back and pin it so the guide moves on
guide.done: That's the tour. No other single move improves your aim.
guide.done.why: The guide stops when no knob it may move improves the aim without risking an out-of-memory failure, or when every useful knob is pinned or already toured.
guide.done.still_failing: None of the knobs I can move clears the memory problem.
guide.pin_blocks_fix: {knob} is pinned, and moving it to {to} is what would fit the run in memory.
guide.pin_blocks_saving: {knob} is pinned. Releasing it to {to} would change {target} by {delta}.
guide.pin_blocks.why: The guide never moves a pinned knob. When the aim can't be met with your pins, it names the pin in the way and what releasing it would buy.
guide.cliff: {knob} at {value} crosses the memory limit: peak {peak}.
guide.rule.eval_batch_size.fix.line: Your eval pass is the out-of-memory risk. An eval batch of {to} instead of {from} brings the peak to {peak}.
guide.rule.eval_batch_size.fix.why: Eval runs every few hundred steps at its own batch size. Here it holds more memory than training does, so the first eval is where the run would die.
guide.rule.eval_batch_size.save.line: An eval batch of {to} changes {target} by {delta}.
guide.rule.eval_batch_size.save.why: Larger eval batches finish evaluation sooner, as long as they still fit beside the training state.
guide.rule.batch_size.fix.line: A batch of {to} instead of {from} fits in memory, and changes {target} by {delta}.
guide.rule.batch_size.fix.why: Activations grow with batch size times sequence length, so halving the batch roughly halves them.
guide.rule.batch_size.save.line: A batch of {to} keeps the GPU busier and changes {target} by {delta}.
guide.rule.batch_size.save.why: Small batches leave the GPU waiting between kernels. A larger batch does more work per launch, until memory runs out.
guide.rule.seq_len.fix.line: Sequences of {to} tokens instead of {from} fit in memory. This changes what the model sees, so check it suits your data.
guide.rule.seq_len.fix.why: Activations and logits grow with sequence length. Shorter sequences fit, but long examples get cut.
guide.rule.grad_ckpt.fix.line: Gradient checkpointing frees activation memory so the run fits. Steps get slower: {target} changes by {delta}.
guide.rule.grad_ckpt.fix.why: Checkpointing keeps only each block's input and recomputes the rest during backward, trading compute for memory.
guide.rule.grad_ckpt.save.why: Checkpointing saves memory at the cost of recomputation. It pays off when the freed memory lets the batch grow.
guide.rule.gpu.fix.line: On {to}, the run fits in memory, and {target} changes by {delta}.
guide.rule.gpu.fix.why: A GPU with more memory removes the limit without touching the code.
guide.rule.gpu.save.line: Is a different GPU worth it? On {to}, {target} changes by {delta}.
guide.rule.gpu.save.why: A pricier GPU can be cheaper overall when it finishes the run fast enough. This one is extrapolated from the spec table, so verify it before you commit.
guide.rule.generic.why: This is the knob whose best single move improves your aim the most, without risking an out-of-memory failure.
